claims.statement: The MCP client keeps one Streamable HTTP session on a tokio runtime, reconnecting every three seconds, and turns `resources/list_changed` into the `dataChanged` signal.
Workspace keys are disabled while a terminal widget has focus.
Opening a page navigates the current page tab unless that tab is pinned; otherwise a new tab opens.
Each terminal is a tmux session with titles forwarded; a title that asks for attention raises a desktop notification once per title and at most once a minute.

The look is a set of colour roles from one of three sources: a built-in preset, the Omarchy desktop theme mapped onto the roles, or a TOML file under `~/.config/rusty/themes/`; `skin::tokens` derives every token the shell and the renderer bind to, the older names included, so no binding knows where a colour came from.
The workspace state (sidebars, panes, expanded folders, the pane's agent) lives in a JSON file the Rust side loads and saves.
Edits autosave one and a half seconds after the last keystroke.
The right sidebar's Tags pane lists every tag as a tree with counts and searches by tag on a click.
The properties block in reading view edits each value by its type through the property tools and adds a key of a chosen type.

The graph view draws `brain_graph`'s nodes and edges on a `Canvas`, laid out by a force simulation (pairwise repulsion, springs on edges, a pull to the centre, damping and cooling) that runs on a 33 ms timer and stops when the layout settles; its filter, group, display and force settings persist in the workspace state under `graph`.
Ctrl+G, the ribbon button and the palette open the global graph as one tab; "Open local graph" on a page opens one local graph tab that follows the last page that was current.

Bookmarks are one JSON array under `bookmarks` in the workspace state, entries of kind file, folder, search or heading with a title; adding one that exists removes it; opening one navigates to the page, reveals the folder, runs the search, or scrolls to the heading once the page has rendered.

The search pane sends the query as typed with `case_sensitive` and `regex` from its two chips and bookmarks the search from a third; Settings renders the palette's command list as the Hotkeys table, the terminal keys added, behind a filter field.

The skin choice (`source`, `name`, `scanlines`) lives under `theme` in the workspace state; a pick in Settings goes through `selectTheme`, which stores it and calls `Theme.select` so every token repaints at once, while the application font is set from the saved skin before the engine loads, so a face change applies at the next launch.

The top bar reads the machine through `Desk` (memory in use, the CPU's share since the last reading, the clock, refreshed every two seconds) and carries the command button and one glyph per agent CLI found on the machine: a click opens the agent in a new tab, a right-click opens it in the agent pane, both as signals the window answers; the Hyprland workspace strip is gone and `Desk` no longer asks the compositor for anything.

The theme carries a base text size (`baseSize`, 12 to 18, default 14, or `RUSTY_TEXT_SIZE` when set, which then wins) and `scale` (`baseSize / 12`); every QML text size is `Math.round(n * theme.scale)` where `n` is the drawn pixel value, the reading view's render style takes its `size` from the same scale and re-renders on a change, and the terminal keeps the Alacritty font at a fixed point size.

The base text size lives as `textSize` in the workspace state, is applied at load, and is set through the window's `setTextSize` by Ctrl with plus, minus and zero (outside a terminal), by three palette commands, and by a stepper under "This machine" in Settings; a Rust test refuses any literal `pixelSize` in the QML and any literal `pointSize` outside the terminal.

The file and folder bookmarks are the favorites: the note header shows a star that toggles the open page's bookmark (Ctrl+D and a palette command do the same), the explorer gathers them in a Favorites section above the tree where a click opens and a right-click removes, and the quick switcher lists them first and starred on an empty query; nothing new is stored.
